items.name: Framework Laptop 13 AMD Ryzen AI 300 Series (exact configuration still to qualify)
items.named_model_or_revision: Framework Laptop 13 AMD Ryzen AI 300 Series; exact RAM, wireless module, board revision and firmware not selected
items.observed_evidence: The official Framework Linux compatibility page lists the Ryzen AI 300 Series model and lists NixOS as community-supported, with Wi-Fi/Bluetooth working out of the box but fingerprint-reader setup required; support differs by generation/configuration. These are vendor compatibility notes, not a Luminous NixOS image or endpoint security qualification. Additional security note: the official NixOS Framework wiki's generic instructions state Secure Boot must be disabled to boot NixOS, while Lanzaboote documents a Framework-specific custom-key enrollment procedure and cautions that behavior varies between notebooks. A signed-boot path is possible to investigate, but the exact board/firmware combination and recovery behavior must be qualified; do not ship an image that depends on Secure Boot being disabled.
open_blockers: Verify current South African ordering, import, warranty, repair and spare-part support; do not infer local stock from the vendor product page.
Choose exact mainboard generation, RAM, wireless module and firmware baseline and pin the deployable configuration.
Qualify secure boot/TPM, firmware update and rollback, IOMMU, sleep/resume, docking, device enrollment and recovery for the intended NixOS profile.
Check lifecycle/support terms, firmware/proprietary binary dependencies, hardware revision changes and replacement-unit reproducibility.

Resolve the observed NixOS Secure Boot path for the exact SKU: demonstrate enrolled keys, signed boot artifacts, vendor firmware update compatibility, dbx handling, rollback, and recovery from a rejected image. Do not treat 'NixOS boots' as evidence that the required boot policy is enforced.

items.name: South African DPSA public-service ICT/security policy index (applicability review required)
items.observed_evidence: The official DPSA standards index lists public-service information-security directive material (2022), a Public Service ICT Security Assessment Standard and checklist (2018), ICT Security Guidelines and service-continuity guidance (2017), MIOS v6, and older policy items including FOSS policy and MISS. The index alone does not establish current applicability to a particular agency, contract or information class.
open_blockers: Retrieve and review the actual signed directive, circulars and current agency ICT/security policies; confirm whether each older standard remains applicable or has been superseded.
Map each applicable requirement to product controls, evidence, procurement clauses, data classification and acceptance tests.
Confirm with the contracting authority whether additional sector-specific, critical-infrastructure, privacy, cryptographic or cross-border requirements apply.

items.name: SITA public-sector ICT hardware and security procurement routes (contract applicability must be checked)
items.observed_evidence: SITA's effective-panel page says listed contracts are available to public bodies, parastatals and organs of state; as viewed 2026-10-10 it lists the information-security products/services panel RFA 2494-2021 ending 2027-09-06 and the server-room/network-cabling related panel RFA 2168-2024 ending 2031-10-10. It also lists UC/VC panel RFA 2501-2021 ending 2026-10-08, which is past the snapshot date and is not treated as current. SITA's hardware page lists RFB 2009 (2026-04-20 to 2027-04-20) and RFB 740 (2025-11-24 to 2026-11-24); actual scope, amendments and category fit must be confirmed against the tender/contract documents. The SITA tender administration listing also showed RFB 3261-2026 for Ethernet switches, wireless LAN, WAN routers, backhaul, copper/fibre cabling and related services with a closing date of 28 August 2026; that date has passed as of this snapshot, so it is historical market evidence rather than an open opportunity. On the official RFQ listing reviewed 2026-10-10, RFQ 6614_2494_2026 (DPSA next-generation firewall, licenses, maintenance and support) and RFQ 6611_2168_2026 (CSPS LAN cabling/server-room maintenance) were listed to close 13 October 2026 at 11:00; RFQ 6615-AH-2026 for Military Health Formation switches/SFPs was listed for 16 October after a compulsory 7 October briefing; RFQ 6619_AH_2026 for SA Army HQ switches/SFPs was listed for 14 October after a compulsory 5 October briefing; and RFQ 6621_2168_2026 for SA Army HQ LAN infrastructure was listed for 30 October with a compulsory briefing scheduled for 16 October. These listing details can change and do not imply bidder eligibility.
open_blockers: Read actual engagement models, technical specifications, terms, accredited-supplier lists and amendments; the public landing page alone is not tender qualification.

Determine whether Luminous should be a product vendor, open-source software supplier, subcontractor, integration partner or supplier through an accredited reseller; none is assumed eligible by this record.
Confirm current contract validity, commodity coverage, licensing terms and procuring authority instructions immediately before any bid or quote.
Prepare commercial support, warranty, SLA, security evidence and local delivery obligations that open-source publication alone does not provide.
Treat tenders whose published closing date has passed as historical only; monitor new calls and verify amendments on the official tender portal.

Verify every deadline, mandatory meeting and eligibility clause in the full live RFQ pack; expired compulsory briefings or prior supplier-panel restrictions can make a listing unusable for a new entrant.

Verify cross-border delivery, customs, warranty and repair support for South Africa.

items.name: Dell PowerEdge T160 near-edge/tower server candidate
items.named_model_or_revision: PowerEdge T160; target quote to specify CPU, TPM 2.0, 32–64 GB ECC UDIMM, storage, NICs, PSU and support
items.observed_evidence: Dell publishes specifications for the T160: ECC UDIMM up to 128 GB, configurable SATA/NVMe storage, TPM 2.0 options, Secure Boot, signed firmware, silicon root of trust, and a dedicated iDRAC port with Redfish/API management. A South African marketplace listing for an E-2414 baseline with 16 GB ECC and 2 TB HDD showed R27,499–R59,799 across sellers on 10 October 2026. That wide variation is not a comparable quote and the baseline is not the recommended security/storage configuration.
open_blockers: Get a supplier quote with exact Dell part number, TPM, memory topology, storage, power supply, warranty and support response time; verify South African service eligibility.
Require a more suitable configuration than a single spinning-disk baseline: evaluate 32–64 GB ECC and redundant enterprise SSDs/boot media, with a separately protected backup target.
Verify NixOS/kernel/storage/NIC compatibility, measured boot and TPM behavior, firmware update/recovery, disk encryption, RAID/HBA mode and exact hardware support.
Place iDRAC on a dedicated isolated management network with unique credentials, MFA where supported, no direct Internet exposure, restricted source IPs and logged access.
Test restore, disk failure, power loss, firmware rollback/recovery, thermal behavior and workload performance on the exact configured unit.

items.name: Production next-generation firewall with contract-backed support (SKU not selected)

Select exact firewall hardware/software SKU, supported throughput with required features enabled, HA options, interface count and update policy.
Assess a vendor-supported product alongside an open-source route; record the operational and lock-in trade-offs without claiming equivalence.
Demonstrate policy enforcement, logging, IPS/DNS filtering if required, VPN performance, failover and security-update response against the actual requirements.

items.name: APC Easy UPS SMV1500AI 230V/1500VA/1050W

The official SMV1500AI-GR variant has four Schuko outlets and a similar displayed price. This is a manufacturer price signal, not a quote, stock guarantee or runtime calculation.

Test UPS USB/serial monitoring with the selected host and NUT/appropriate daemon, including low-battery shutdown ordering.
Test mains loss, brownout, battery self-test failure, alerting, graceful shutdown and recovery; verify serviceable battery lifecycle.
